Consensus sequence of each sample

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/consensus-sequences.R
consensusSequences.Rd

Builds, for every sample of a WithinHostExperiment, the reference sequence with each substitution present at or above minFreq written in, and returns the sequences as a DNAStringSet. Its purpose is comparison between hosts: the within-host ratio of pNpSWithinHost describes polymorphism inside one host, whereas dN/dS between hosts is a divergence between their consensus sequences, which the models of MSA2dist::dnastring2kaks() estimate.

Usage

consensusSequences(x, ref, ...)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment,DNAStringSet'
consensusSequences(
  x,
  ref,
  minFreq = 0.5,
  usePassedOnly = TRUE,
  seqname = NULL,
  region = NULL,
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment,character'
consensusSequences(x, ref, ...)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment,XString'
consensusSequences(x, ref, ...)

Arguments

x

A WithinHostExperiment with ref and alt columns in mcols(rowRanges(x)).

ref

A DNAStringSet holding the reference sequence the variants were called against, for example from Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(). Sequence names are cut at the first space.

...

Not used; supplying anything is an error.

minFreq

Numeric scalar in (0, 1]. The frequency at or above which a substitution is written in (default 0.5).

usePassedOnly

Logical. If TRUE (default), only sites with qcPass == TRUE in that sample are written in.

seqname

The sequence of ref to build; required when ref holds more than one sequence and region does not name one.

region

Optional GRanges on seqname, all on one strand: the part of the sequence to return; see Details.

Value

A DNAStringSet with one sequence per sample, named by sample. Its mcols() hold n_substitutions, the number of substitutions written into the returned part of each sequence.

Details

Only substitutions are written in: single-nucleotide changes and multi-nucleotide changes whose reference and alternative alleles have the same length. Insertions and deletions are not applied, with a warning, so every consensus has the length of the reference and stays aligned to it and to every other sample's consensus; that is what MSA2dist::dnastring2kaks() needs. Where a deletion or insertion is fixed in a host, the returned sequence therefore differs from that host's true consensus.

A site enters a sample's consensus when its altFreq is at least minFreq and, with usePassedOnly = TRUE, it passed QC. With minFreq at or below 0.5 two alleles can qualify at one position; the more frequent is written in, the first in the object on a tie, and a warning reports how many were set aside. A site whose ref allele differs from the reference at that position is never written in, with a warning, since it was called against another sequence.

region restricts the output to part of the sequence, such as one coding sequence: its ranges are taken in order along the sequence and joined, and the result is reverse-complemented when they lie on the minus strand, so a coding sequence split into parts comes back as one sequence read in its own direction. Positions are those of the reference, since no length-changing edit is made.

See also

pNpSWithinHost for the within-host ratio; MSA2dist::dnastring2kaks() for dN/dS between sequences.

Examples

## A coding sequence of 15 codons and three hosts, each carrying one
## synonymous and one nonsynonymous change at high frequency:
## host1 6 G>A (CTG -> CTA) and 7 A>G (AAA -> GAA),
## host2 12 G>A (GGG -> GGA) and 13 T>C (TTT -> CTT),
## host3 18 C>A (CCC -> CCA) and 19 A>C (AAA -> CAA)
ref <- Biostrings::DNAStringSet(c(
    seg1 = "ATGCTGAAAGGGTTTCCCAAACTGATGGTTCTGAAAGGGTTTTAA"))
gr <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("seg1",
    IRanges::IRanges(c(6, 7, 12, 13, 18, 19), width = 1))
S4Vectors::mcols(gr)$ref <- c("G", "A", "G", "T", "C", "A")
S4Vectors::mcols(gr)$alt <- c("A", "G", "A", "C", "A", "C")
freqs <- cbind(host1 = c(0.95, 0.91, 0.02, 0.03, 0.01, 0.02),
               host2 = c(0.03, 0.02, 0.88, 0.93, 0.04, 0.01),
               host3 = c(0.01, 0.04, 0.02, 0.01, 0.97, 0.90))
whe <- WithinHostExperiment(
    assays = list(altFreq = freqs),
    rowRanges = gr,
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(sample_id = colnames(freqs),
                                   row.names = colnames(freqs)))
cons <- consensusSequences(whe, ref)
cons
#> DNAStringSet object of length 3:
#>     width sequence                                          names               
#> [1]    45 ATGCTAGAAGGGTTTCCCAAACTGATGGTTCTGAAAGGGTTTTAA     host1
#> [2]    45 ATGCTGAAAGGACTTCCCAAACTGATGGTTCTGAAAGGGTTTTAA     host2
#> [3]    45 ATGCTGAAAGGGTTTCCACAACTGATGGTTCTGAAAGGGTTTTAA     host3

## dN/dS between the hosts' consensus coding sequences: every pair
## differs by two synonymous and two nonsynonymous changes
if (requireNamespace("MSA2dist", quietly = TRUE)) {
    kaks <- suppressMessages(MSA2dist::dnastring2kaks(cons, model = "Li"))
    kaks[, c("seq1", "seq2", "Ka", "Ks", "Ka/Ks")]
}
#>    seq1  seq2         Ka        Ks     Ka/Ks
#> 1 host1 host2 0.07421000 0.1786266 0.4154477
#> 2 host1 host3 0.06400214 0.2538504 0.2521254
#> 3 host2 host3 0.06436570 0.2384559 0.2699270
